newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMAN WINTER BARLEY HARVEST NEARLY COMPLETE - ZMP.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN WINTER BARLEY HARVEST NEARLY COMPLETE - ZMP.

text.p: German winter barley harvests are mostly done, the farm price office ZMP said on Friday
Between 10 and 60 percent of rye and triticale, a wheat/rye hybrid, and 25 percent of malting barley had also been cut, it said in a report.
Rye prices from the harvest were below those of wheat because a tendency towards low falling numbers, which indicate baking qualities, meant much material was offered as feed.
Millers were offering to pay 240 marks for bread rye in North-Rhine-Westphalia.
Wheat harvesting has started in the south and west, with other regions due to begin their harvests next week or later.
Wheat results in the western states of Rhineland-Palatinate and Saar varied greatly, with protein content unsatisfactory.
But they were far better in Hesse, Baden and Bavaria, the major producer with more than three million tonnes of winter wheat last year, where falling numbers were also positive.
The barley harvest in Lower Saxony -- with 1.25 million the second largest German producer after Bavaria last year -- showed yields 10 to 15 percent above those last year.
With yields in North-Rhine Westphalia, the third largest producer, also high, ex-farm prices in these states were looking set to fall below their current range of 200-210 marks a tonne.
Price indications from the Baden region, where volumes and qualities were also excellent, were already at 180-200 marks.
Malting barley qualities, although not as high as last year, were still looking satisfactory to consumers, and supply should be ample from a slightly lower area in 1997.
